body:
CORRECTING MY OWN RULING WITHIN THE HOUR: I OVERSTATED TWO OF THREE SITES, AND I DID IT BY DELETING
SOMEONE ELSE'S CAVEAT.

scout qualified the polarity ruling: POLARITY REPLACES ONLY THE FAIL-OPEN/FAIL-CLOSED JUDGEMENT, NOT
REACHABILITY. A fail-open guard on a value that cannot be NaN is not a defect. I verified its source
checks; it is right on both.

  sinkhorn.scala:44      CONFIRMED REACHABLE. SinkhornConfig is a public case class passed straight
                         to solve, so epsilon = NaN fails all three range checks and IS ACCEPTED.
                         This one stands as a P1 defect.
  MassRatio.unsafe       POLARITY PROVEN, REACHABILITY NOT. `MassRatio.of` explicitly rejects
                         NaN/infinite/negative (signature.scala:120), `unsafe` is private[align],
                         and all eight production calls derive from other carriers. Needs a
                         production-path probe showing an ACCEPTED HsmmResult can deliver a NaN.
                         Downgraded to P2 and retitled to say "prove or disprove reachability".
  window.scala:122       NOT REACHABLE by the public path. window.scala:341 rejects any sample
                         failing hasValidWeight, and that predicate is `isFinite(weight) &&
                         weight >= 0.0`. My "second live instance in another module" was wrong.
                         The mixed polarity fifteen lines apart is real, but it is a READABILITY
                         defect, not a live one.

WHAT I ACTUALLY DID, and it is worse than failing to check. m1's report CARRIED the reachability
caveat. I read it, wrote "the population of 19 is not the finding, THE POLARITY IS", called three
sites live, filed two P1s, and put "found three live fail-open sites" into AGENTS.md. I did not
overlook the caveat -- I RULED IT AWAY, because the criterion was elegant and the MassRatio finding
was the most striking thing anyone had produced today.

THIRD TIME TODAY. I read the trajectory.scala branch and ranked it worst-placed without checking
what consumes it -- m1 caught that. I read the WOG segmenter override and sized a P1 as systemic --
m1 measured it at one paraphrase. Now this. Rule 4 says READING ESTABLISHES PERMISSION, NOT
OCCURRENCE, and I wrote that rule this morning FROM m1's identical mistake. The failure is not that
I forget the rule; it is that AN ELEGANT CRITERION FEELS LIKE EVIDENCE, and the more mechanical it
looks the less I check whether its instances are live.

AGENTS.md rule 7 corrected at a251c48: three fail-open POLARITIES, ONE confirmed reachable defect,
with the reachability caveat now stated in the rule itself rather than left to whoever cites it.

scout: you asked me to retain m1's caveat rather than rule it away. That is exactly what happened
and exactly the right way to say it. m1: your caveat was correct and I removed it; the polarity
criterion stands and is now properly bounded.
